messages.content: You check each debater against its own earlier words. You bring nothing from outside the words given to you: no doctrine, no training knowledge, no reading of your own. You do not judge who is right, and you do not judge one side by the other side's words.

You are the closing enforcer. A debater's closing round may not contradict what the same debater stated in its earlier rounds. Below are one debater's four rounds.
Read its closing round against its earlier rounds. List every closing sentence that cannot be true together with an earlier sentence, and answer every candidate listed.
A contradiction is two statements that cannot both be true. A closing sentence that asserts again, as the debater's own, what it withdrew, dropped or gave up in an earlier round IS a contradiction.
It is NOT a contradiction when the closing sentence: grants, concedes, narrows or withdraws something; states or quotes the other side's position; answers a press with a further reason the earlier sentence leaves room for; or differs only in wording.
Quote both sentences word for word and name the link: the link whose closing block holds the sentence, else the link the earlier sentence supports.
Reply with one line per contradiction and per candidate, and nothing else:
CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: <candidate id or NEW> -- <DEFENDER|CHALLENGER> -- LINK <n> -- CONFIRMED | NOT A CONTRADICTION -- EARLIER [<round>] "<words>" -- CLOSING [<round 4>] "<words>" -- <one sentence: why both cannot be true, or why they can>
If you find none and there is no candidate, reply: CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NONE

CANDIDATES ALREADY NAMED (answer each one by its id):
A43 -- DEFENDER -- LINK (you name it) -- EARLIER [CR2] "Elisabeth's impossibility was barrenness and age." -- CLOSING [CR4] "It is the immediate seed, Solomon." -- named by the anti-cheat check: Luke 1:36

######## THE DEFENDER ########
The defender's links: D1 = LINK 1, D2 = LINK 2, D3 = LINK 3, D4 = LINK 4, D5 = LINK 5, D6 = LINK 6 (its DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1]). Its closing round is [CR4].

=== [CR1] ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** Christ's conception was not by a man. By "biological father" I mean the man whose seed begets the child. The KJV names one source for the conception, the Holy Ghost, and it names a woman who "know[s] not a man." Joseph is Mary's husband and the child's guardian, but he is not the one who begot him.

---

## 1. The conception took place before any union

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] The Greek *prin ē synelthein autous* means "before they came together." *Synerchomai* (G4905) means to come together. The text sets the conception before the union. The phrase *ek pneumatos hagiou* means "out of the Holy Ghost." *Ek* (G1537) marks source or origin.

[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The word "till" carries the non-union through the whole pregnancy to the birth.

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the union, and Matthew 1:25 keeps the union from happening until after the birth. The only source named for the pregnancy is *ek pneumatos hagiou*. So no union with Joseph (or any man) lies behind the conception.

## 2. The angel names the source

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] *To en autē gennēthen* means "that which is begotten in her." *Gennaō* (G1080) is the verb used of a father begetting and of a mother bearing. The origin is again *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Ghost." The "for" (*gar*) gives the reason Joseph should not fear. Joseph's fear is about the child's origin, and the answer is the Holy Ghost.

[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] *Epeleusetai* means "shall come upon." *Episkiasei* means "shall overshadow." The "therefore" (*dio*) makes the conception by the Holy Ghost the reason the child is called the Son of God.

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:20 names the source of the begetting (*ek*), and Luke 1:35 names the agent and the result. Both texts name the Holy Ghost as the one acting. Neither gives a place to a man's seed. [L3] Hebrews 10:5 says, "a body hast thou prepared me." The Greek *katartizō* (G2675) means to fit or prepare. The body is described as prepared by God.

## 3. Mary's own testimony

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," is used here of sexual relations. The Hebrew *yāda'* (H3045) is used the same way. [L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain."

[L4] Footing: Luke 1:34 uses "know" in the sense Genesis 4:1 shows, where "knew" leads to "conceived." Mary says she has not known a man. The answer she receives in Luke 1:35 gives the Holy Ghost as the way it will be, and does not point to a man. [L3] Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Luke 1:31 says "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

## 4. Joseph is not the one who begat

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] Every earlier line in the genealogy uses *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," with a man as subject. In verse 16 the pattern changes. The relative *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular. *Egennēthē* is passive, "was born." Joseph is called *anēr* (G435), "husband," of Mary. The text does not say "Joseph begat Jesus."

[L3] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." [L2] *Dikaios* (G1342) means righteous or just. [L4] Footing: Joseph is called just in Matthew 1:19, and in Matthew 1:20 the angel reassures him about taking Mary, which shows he did not take himself to be the father. His intent to put her away fits a man who knows the child is not his.

[L3] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." [L2] *Enomizeto* (G3543) means "was thought" or "was reckoned." The KJV marks Joseph's fatherhood as the supposition of others. [L3] Luke 2:48–49: Mary says "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The child answers, "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" The child does not accept Joseph as the father in that sense.

## 5. The sign

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

[L2] The Hebrew is *'almāh* (H5959), the word the KJV renders "virgin." [L3] Genesis 24:43 uses *'almāh* of Rebekah, and Genesis 24:16 describes her as "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

[L1] Matthew 1:22–23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet… Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." [L2] Matthew's Greek is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."

[L4] Footing: Isaiah 7:14 calls the conception a "sign" from the Lord. Matthew 1:22–23 ties the fulfilment to Mary with the word "virgin." A conception by a man would not be a sign.

## 6. What the supposed father texts do and do not show

[L1] Luke 4:22: "Is not this Joseph's son?" [L1] John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." These are the speech of the crowd and of Philip. [L3] Luke 3:23 marks that belief as "as was supposed," and Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 give the truth about the source.

[L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." [L3] Luke 1:31–32: the child is conceived in Mary's womb and receives "the throne of his father David." [L3] Matthew 1:20–21, 25: Joseph, "son of David," takes Mary as his wife and names the child, so the child is reckoned in his house. [L4] Footing: Luke 1:31–32 ties David's promise to the child born of Mary, and Matthew 1:20–25 shows Joseph's role as receiving and naming. Neither requires Joseph's seed. The "flesh" of Romans 1:3 is the body born of the woman (Luke 1:35, "born of thee").

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. The conception was before any union of Mary and Joseph. [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost"; [L2] *prin ē synelthein autous* (before they came together) and *ek* (out of, source); [L3] Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
2. The Holy Ghost is named as the source and agent of the conception. [L1] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"; [L2] *gennēthen* (begotten) with *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Ghost); [L3] Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee… therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
3. Mary had not known a man, and the answer to her question names the Holy Ghost, not a man. [L1] Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man"; [L2] *ginōskō* (to know, of sexual relations); [L3] Genesis 4:1 "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
4. Joseph is called husband, not the one who begat. [L1] Matthew 1:16 "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus"; [L2] *hēs* (of whom, feminine) with *egennēthē* (was born) after the repeated *egennēsen* (begat); [L3] Luke 3:23 "as was supposed the son of Joseph" (*enomizeto*, was thought).
5. The conception was the sign of virgin conception foretold. [L1] Isaiah 7:14 "a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son"; [L2] *'almāh* (the word the KJV renders "virgin") with *parthenos* (virgin); [L3] Matthew 1:22–23 "that it might be fulfilled… a virgin shall be with child."
6. Therefore Christ had no human biological father. [L4] Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:20 name the Holy Ghost as the only source; [L1] Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25 deny union with a man; [L3] Luke 1:35 gives the reason for the title "the Son of God."

=== [CR2] ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 2, RESPONSE

# ROUND 2: DEFENDER'S REPLY

I answer the question first, then C1 through C4, then the six premises. Where I grant a row, I do not rest on it afterward.

---

## THE QUESTION: How is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14)?

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
[L2] *Prodēlos* (G4271) means "plain before all men, i.e. obvious." The tribe is plain in public reckoning. *Anatellō* (G393) means "to (cause to) arise." It is the verb of rising, not of begetting.

[L3] Luke 2:4-5: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David" and went up "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child." The public record is Joseph's house, with Mary enrolled in it.
[L3] Matthew 1:21, 25: "thou shalt call his name JESUS"; "and he called his name JESUS." The child is placed in Joseph's house by name.

The law reckons a house by name and by law, apart from begetting:
- [L3] Deuteronomy 25:6: "the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother [which is] dead."
- [L3] Genesis 48:5: "as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine."
- [L3] Ruth 4:17: "There is a son born to Naomi."

[L4] Hebrews 7:14 makes the tribe obvious (G4271), and Luke 2:4-5 and Matthew 1:21, 25 supply the public house-record. Deuteronomy 25:6 and Genesis 48:5 show Israel reckoning sons into a house by name and law. So the tribe is evident by Joseph's house-reckoning without Joseph's seed.

A second line is open. [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli." [L3] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph." [L4] The KJV's brackets mark "[the son]" as supplied, and the two Gospels name different fathers for Joseph, Jacob and Heli. [L3] Luke 3:33, "which was [the son] of Juda," puts Judah in the line Luke gives. Either way the answer to the question requires no seed of Joseph.

---

## C1: "the seed comes out of a man's body"

[L1] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ."
[L2] *Osphys* (G3751) means "the loin... procreative power." *Anistēmi* (G450) means "to raise up." The subject of the raising is God (*theos*, G2316).
[L3] Acts 13:23: "Of this man's seed hath God according to [his] promise raised unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus."
[L3] Hebrews 7:9-10: "Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham." "For he was yet in the loins of his father."

[L4] Hebrews 7:10 places Levi in Abraham's loins across intervening generations. So "of the loins of David" (Acts 2:30) is descent from David across many generations. It does not name the next begetter. Acts 2:30 and Acts 13:23 make God the one who raises up (G450) from David's seed. The challenger's step from "loins of David" to "loins of Joseph" is the link that has no footing.

[L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
[L2] The verb is *ginomai* (G1096), "to become, be made." Matthew's verb for a father begetting is *gennaō*, "begat" (Matthew 1:16).
[L4] Romans 1:3 uses the verb of becoming, with *sperma* (G4690) for the line. Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 use *gennaō* and *ek* for the source of the conception, and both name the Holy Ghost. I do not rest this on Galatians 4:4. The idiom there is said of men with fathers (Job 14:1; Matthew 11:11), and I grant that.

---

## C2 and C3: the father's house, and "four voices"

[L2] Luke 3:23's *enomizeto* (G3543) is, as the challenger grants, "to do by law (usage)." [L4] That grant supports me. It shows Joseph's fatherhood reckoned by law and usage, which is the footing of the house-reckoning above (Deuteronomy 25:6). It does not make him the begetter.

[L1] Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
[L4] Gabriel calls David "his father" across many generations (Matthew 1:1-16). In the KJV, "father" therefore covers the one from whose house a man is reckoned. So Luke 2:48 "thy father" fits a father by house and law.

Each voice, taken in turn:
- [L1] Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled." The narrator who wrote "his parents" at Luke 2:41 writes "Joseph" and "his mother" here, and writes "as was supposed" at Luke 3:23.
- [L3] John 6:42: "whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" The crowd's "we know" is set against his claim, and the same crowd's mouth is Luke 4:22.
- [L3] Luke 2:48-49: Mary says "thy father and I." The child answers "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The challenger's reply passed over Luke 2:49. It stands as the child's own answer to "thy father," and it is unanswered.

---

## C4 (the keystone): "Joseph knew Mary within the espousal"

**The conception is dated before the taking.**
[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] *Gennēthen* (the KJV margin says "Gr. begotten") is a perfect-sense participle: the child is already begotten in her when the angel speaks. *Gar* gives the reason for "fear not."

[L4] The challenger's chain needs the knowing to fall before the taking. Matthew 1:18 states "the birth... was on this wise," and the manner it gives is "before they came together... found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20 gives the child as already begotten while the taking is still future ("fear not to take"). So Matthew's own account of how the birth came about places the begetting before the taking, with the Holy Ghost as its source.

**Joseph's intent, met on its meaning.**
[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man]... was minded to put her away privily."
[L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: the law for a betrothed damsel with another man says "so thou shalt put away evil from among you."
[L4] I accept that she is "Joseph her husband's" betrothed wife (Matthew 1:19-20; Deuteronomy 22:24). The question is what moves a husband to put her away. A husband who had begotten the child would have no cause to put her away. Matthew 1:18 says she was "found" with child. Matthew 1:19 shows the finding as a cause for putting her away. So Joseph read the pregnancy as not his. The angel answers that fear with the source: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). The reason given (*gar*) is the source, and it is not "the child is yours." The challenger replied that "both rows sit inside C4." That does not meet what the verse says about Joseph's reading of the pregnancy.

**"Till."**
[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
[L4] I grant that "till" bounds the abstaining from the taking to the birth. What gives Matthew 1:25 its force is its connection with Matthew 1:18 and 1:20. Together they say before the union "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost," and the verse that follows says Joseph did not know her until the birth.

---

## The D-links the challenger pressed

**D2: "of God" said of believers.**
[L1] John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
[L2] *Ek theou* (out of God) is set against *ek thelēmatos andros* (out of the will of a male man, G435). [L4] The phrase the challenger cites sets "of God" against "the will of man." It therefore gives no footing for "of the Holy Ghost" with a man's seed also in the child. And [L1] Matthew 1:20 speaks of what "is conceived in her," a child in a womb. Believers in 1 John 5:1 are not conceived in a womb.

**"Come upon" and "overshadow."**
[L1] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L3] Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses." In Acts the result is witnesses. In Luke 1:35 the same coming is followed by "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." [L4] The verse itself joins the Spirit's coming to a birth.
[L2] *Dio* means "wherefore," and it is a reason-word tied to what precedes it in the same sentence. [L4] The antecedent of "therefore also" is "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." The challenger sends it back to Luke 1:32. That cuts the clause from its own sentence.
[L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." The ground of Solomon's sonship is choice. The ground of Luke 1:35's sonship is "therefore," from a conception.

**D3: Elisabeth.**
[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L3] Luke 1:36-37: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age"; "For with God nothing shall be impossible." [L3] Luke 1:7: "because that Elisabeth was barren." Elisabeth's impossibility was barrenness and age. Mary's impossibility is that she "know[s] not a man," and the angel's ground in Luke 1:37 is that nothing is impossible with God. A betrothed virgin who is soon to wed a husband would not ask "how" if the way were the husband. Her "how" shows the angel is announcing something other than the ordinary way (Luke 1:31, 35).

**D5: Isaiah 7:14.**
[L1] Isaiah 7:11: "Ask thee a sign of the LORD thy God; ask [it] either in the depth, or in the height above." [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive."
[L2] *'Almāh* (H5959) is the word the challenger counts as "7 verses." Genesis 24:43 is one of them, and the KJV renders it there "the virgin." [L3] Genesis 24:16 (*bethulah*) says of the same Rebekah "neither had any man known her."
[L3] Isaiah 8:3: the prophet "went unto the prophetess; and she conceived," and the name is "Mahershalalhashbaz." Isaiah 7:14 gives the name "Immanuel." [L4] The two children bear different names and have different mothers, a prophetess and a virgin. [L1] Matthew 1:22-23 says "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled... Behold, a virgin shall be with child." "All this" includes Matthew 1:18-21, the conception of the Holy Ghost.

**D6 (premise 1, Mary's house).**
[L1] Luke 1:31-32: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb... the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The David promise is addressed to Mary about the child "in thy womb."
[L1] Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same." [L4] Hebrews 2:17 says "like unto [his] brethren" in flesh and blood. It places likeness in the flesh. It does not give a means of conceiving.

---

## WHERE THE CHAIN STANDS

1. Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 date the begetting before the taking and name the Holy Ghost as its source. The challenger's C4 needs the knowing before the taking, and no quoted row gives it.
2. Hebrews 7:14, Acts 2:30, Acts 13:23 and Hebrews 7:10 are all met by house-reckoning and descent across generations, with God as the one who raises up. None needs Joseph's seed.
3. Luke 2:49 and John 1:13 remain unmet in the challenger's reply.

=== [CR3] ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097) means "to know." It stands in Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
[L3] Ruth 4:13: "So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception."

I grant that she was Joseph's wife in law during the espousal, and that "came together" (1:18) is the taking home. The chain does not need more than that.
1. Matthew 1:18 sets the finding "before they came together." The conception is already stated as "of the Holy Ghost" at the finding.
2. Ruth 4:13, the challenger's own row, sets the order as taking first ("Boaz took Ruth") and going in after ("when he went in unto her").
3. Matthew 1:24 gives the taking ("took unto him his wife") and Matthew 1:25 gives the knowing bounded to the birth ("knew her not till").
4. Genesis 4:1 puts the knowing before the conceiving: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." In Matthew the order is reversed. The child is already "conceived in her" (1:20) before the taking (1:24), and the knowing is withheld after it (1:25).

[L4] So by the challenger's own pattern in Genesis 4:1 and Ruth 4:13, no knowing by Joseph stands before the conception. The press on Matthew 1:24, Deuteronomy 22:24 and Genesis 4:1 grants the wife-status. It does not show a knowing before the finding.

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
[L2] *Gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate, to beget." It stands behind Matthew 1:20, where the KJV margin gives "begotten."
[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**John 1:13, 1 John 5:1, 1 John 3:9.** The subjects there are "as many as received him" (John 1:12) and "Whosoever believeth" (1 John 5:1). Believing is named, so the begetting is of the new kind. In Matthew 1:20 the one begotten is "that which is conceived in her." No believing is named, and the margin gives "begotten" for the womb's conception. The press fits believers and does not reach a child in the womb.

**John 3:6.** "that which is born of the Spirit is spirit" names the Spirit as the source. Matthew 1:20 names the same source for the conception.

**Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34.**
- Acts 1:8 ends in "ye shall be witnesses." Luke 1:35 ends in "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- The same coming-upon and overshadowing are followed by a thing born of Mary, not a witness.
- Luke 1:35 adds "the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee," and it answers "How shall this be" (Luke 1:34).

**Luke 1:32 and the "therefore."**
- Luke 1:32 gives the title: "shall be called the Son of the Highest."
- Luke 1:35 states a ground for that title after Mary asks how. The ground is the coming and overshadowing, and the thing "born of thee."
- The same title is given twice, and the second time it carries a reason.

**1 Chronicles 28:6 and 2 Samuel 7:14.** There the sonship is by choice: "I have chosen him [to be] my son." In Luke 1:35 the ground is the thing born by the overshadowing.

[L4] So the Holy Ghost is named as the one acting in the conception (Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35).

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know"), present tense, is her state at that hour.
[L3] Genesis 24:16: "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

I grant the present tense. It is her state, and she names that state as the ground of "how."
1. Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin espoused." Her espousal is already stated, and her question is still "How shall this be."
2. The angel's reply names the Holy Ghost coming upon her (1:35). The reply names no man.

**Elisabeth (Luke 1:36-37).**
- The barrenness and age are stated in Luke 1:7: "Elisabeth was barren, and they both were [now] well stricken in years."
- The reply to Zacharias names the husband: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13).
- The reply to Mary says "born of thee" (Luke 1:35), with no "bear thee."
- Verse 37 follows the naming of the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest.

**Luke 1:32 and 2 Samuel 7:12.** These state what is promised ("the throne of his father David"). Mary's question asks how, and the answer to how is Luke 1:35.

[L4] So the angel's answer gives the Holy Ghost where the husband would stand for Zacharias (Luke 1:13).

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L2] *Paradeigmatizō* (G3856) means "to make a public example."
[L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "ye shall stone them with stones that they die... because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife."

I grant the verse's stated grounds: justice, and unwillingness to expose her. The press says the cause is public shame whoever the begetter was. The verse's own words meet that.
1. A "publick example" is the stoning at the gate of Deuteronomy 22:24, and that law falls on a betrothed wife humbled by another man.
2. A husband who knew the child was his own would have no such example to avoid. The ground "not willing to make her a publick example" is a ground only for a man who took the child to be another's.
3. The angel answers with a reason: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). The "for" names the child's source, not the shame, as the reason to take her.

**Luke 2:48 and Luke 3:23.**

## Closing

D1 stands on Matthew 1:18, where the finding comes before the coming together. D2 stands on Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, the Holy Ghost as stated source with "therefore also". D3 stands on Luke 1:34-35. D4 stands on Matthew 1:16 and Luke 3:23, where the begetting verb ends before Jesus. D5 stands on Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23. D6 follows: the text names the Holy Ghost as the source and gives Joseph the title "husband", so Christ had no human biological father. Every witness the challenger pressed has been named and answered above.
